name: docker-asterisk
what_it_is: A Dockerized Asterisk PBX image based on Alpine Linux, bundling the PrivateDial configuration suite, WebSMS HTTP-to-SMS bridge, and AutoBan intrusion detection via nftables. Targets residential and small-office VoIP deployments with TLS/SRTP media encryption and multi-stage image variants.
components: PrivateDial – custom dialplan/config suite for voice, video, IM/SMS, and voicemail-by-email
WebSMS – PHP-based HTTP API bridge for SMS when SIP MESSAGE is unsupported by provider
AutoBan – intrusion detection/prevention daemon monitoring AMI security events and blocking IPs via nftables
PulseAudio integration (full/xtra variants) – two-way container audio via host socket sharing
runit init scheme – multi-service supervision under /etc/service/
docker-entrypoint.sh – entry/exit script lifecycle with SIGTERM handler
protocols: SRTP with SDES or DTLS key exchange
AMI – Asterisk Manager Interface (internal, used by AutoBan)
measurement: Configurable log level via SYSLOG_LEVEL (0-8 scale); logs directed to Docker daemon
AMI event stream consumed by AutoBan for security event monitoring
Health check mechanism present (details in image; not fully documented in README)
State persistence via entry/exit scripts in /etc/docker/entry.d and /etc/docker/exit.d
configuration: Environment variable SYSLOG_LEVEL (default 4, range 0-8) controls logging verbosity
HOSTNAME – used for TLS certificate CN identification
ACME_FILE (default /acme/acme.json) – path to Let's Encrypt cert from Traefik
ACME_POSTHOOK (default 'sv restart asterisk') – command run after certificate update
WEBSMSD_PORT (default 80; unset = WebSMS disabled) – PHP web server port
PULSE_SERVER / PULSE_COOKIE – PulseAudio socket and auth token for host audio
Config files seeded to /etc/asterisk on first start; existing configs untouched on upgrade
All persistent config consolidated under /srv with symlinks from standard Asterisk paths
RTP port range configurable in rtp.conf; must be narrowed (e.g., 10000-10099) in bridge network mode
Non-standard SIP ports supported via config for security obscurity
fault_injection: AutoBan blocks IPs via nftables on repeated SIP authentication failures detected through AMI
Requires cap_add: [net_admin, net_raw] for nftables manipulation inside container
No explicit fault-injection test harness documented
modes: base – Asterisk + TLS + logging + WebSMS + AutoBan
Docker networking: bridge mode (default) or host mode (bypasses docker-proxy, loses bridge isolation)
constraints: Docker bridge networking cannot publish port ranges; RTP range must be narrowed significantly (e.g., 100 ports) or --network host must be used
TLS provides hop-by-hop signaling encryption only; end-to-end media encryption is a known design limitation
ICE/STUN/TURN configuration is explicitly noted as out of scope in the documentation
AutoBan requires net_admin and net_raw Linux capabilities; may conflict with restrictive container security policies
Self-signed certificates are regenerated if validity falls below TLS_CERTDAYS threshold, requiring client trust configuration
docker_services: asterisk – main PBX service (mlan/asterisk image, variants: mini/base/full/xtra/latest); ports 5060/udp, 5060/tcp, 5061/tcp, 10000-10099/udp (typical narrowed RTP range); volumes for /srv (config persistence) and optionally /acme (Let's Encrypt); cap_add: [sys_ptrace, net_admin, net_raw]
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml at repo root (only inline examples in README)
No built-in metrics exporter (e.g., Prometheus endpoint) documented
ICE/STUN/TURN configuration guidance explicitly out of scope
No CLI-based dynamic port range configuration (requires file edits)
No multi-node clustering or high-availability configuration documented
